en: One milliliter of liquid water expands to form about 1,700 milliliters of steam when boiled at 100 degrees Celsius.
A solid block of osmium the size of a standard one-liter milk carton weighs approximately 22.6 kilograms.
One liter of average seawater contains about 35 grams of dissolved salt, which equals roughly seven teaspoons.
Solid gallium metal melts at 29.76 degrees Celsius, meaning it will turn into a liquid just by holding it.
When iron undergoes a chemical change to form rust, it expands in volume by up to six times.
The highly viscous liquid called pitch flows so slowly that it takes about ten years to form one drop.
Diamond scores a perfect ten on the Mohs hardness scale, making it much harder than talc, which scores one.
You can dissolve 2,000 grams of sugar in one liter of cold water, but nearly 5,000 grams in boiling water.
Carbon dioxide gas is about 1.5 times denser than regular air, causing it to sink and pool near the floor.
Liquid nitrogen boils at minus 196 degrees Celsius, which is 196 degrees colder than the freezing point of pure water.
The Eiffel Tower grows about 15 centimeters taller during hot summer days because its iron structure undergoes thermal expansion.
Pure gold is so malleable that just two grams can be hammered into a flat sheet covering one square meter.
